messages.content: I need to sort out flights for a St. Louis installation. The condition review is Tuesday, July 21 at 1:00 p.m., and the installation is Wednesday, July 22. They expect to finish around 5:00 p.m., but that could slip.

I can compare the practical combinations from Atlanta. Are you deciding between arriving Monday evening and taking an early nonstop Tuesday, and between returning Wednesday evening and Thursday morning? Also, which St. Louis museum should I use for the airport transfer estimate?
Yes. It is the Saint Louis Art Museum in Forest Park. I will be traveling alone. I need enough time to get from the airport to the museum without turning the review into a close call.

For a 1:00 p.m. review, I would allow roughly 25 to 35 minutes from St. Louis Lambert Airport to the museum by car in ordinary midday traffic, plus time to deplane and collect anything checked. A Tuesday nonstop arriving before about 9:30 a.m. would provide a reasonable buffer; anything later would make the same-day plan less resilient. I’ll compare that with a Monday evening arrival and check the return options after 5:00 p.m. Wednesday.
Please do. I do not need the cheapest possible ticket if the schedule is materially safer, but I want to see the difference.

The strongest outbound choices I found are a Delta nonstop Monday, July 20, leaving ATL at 6:10 p.m. and arriving STL at 6:52 p.m. for $318 round trip when paired with a Thursday return, or a Delta nonstop Tuesday, July 21, leaving at 7:05 a.m. and arriving at 7:46 a.m. for $336 round trip. The Tuesday flight leaves more than five hours before the review, but a cancellation or substantial delay would leave little recovery time. The Monday flight gives you the evening in St. Louis and removes that exposure, at the cost of another hotel night.
What is available Wednesday night? I would rather understand whether that return is genuinely workable before adding Thursday night to the comparison.

There is a Delta nonstop Wednesday at 7:10 p.m., arriving Atlanta at 9:45 p.m. It would require leaving the museum around 5:25 p.m. to maintain a sensible airport buffer. If installation ends exactly at 5:00 p.m., that is possible; if sign-off, packing records, or a delayed finish keeps you past about 5:30, it becomes tight. A later one-stop itinerary leaves at 8:35 p.m. and reaches Atlanta at 12:41 a.m., but its connection makes it less attractive and it does not create much useful margin.
So the 7:10 only works if everyone stays on schedule. What are the Thursday morning nonstops?

Thursday, July 23 has Delta nonstops at 7:00 a.m., arriving Atlanta at 9:34 a.m., and 9:15 a.m., arriving at 11:49 a.m. Paired with the Monday evening outbound, the 7:00 a.m. return is $318 round trip and the 9:15 a.m. return is $347. Paired with Tuesday morning, they are $336 and $365 respectively. All four fares are standard economy and currently allow advance seat selection; a checked bag would be additional unless covered separately.
Compare the two ends independently. How much time does Monday evening really buy me, and how much does Thursday morning buy after the installation?

Monday evening buys the larger operational benefit. You would reach the hotel around 7:45 to 8:15 p.m., then have Tuesday morning available before the 1:00 p.m. review. The Tuesday flight is scheduled early enough, but it concentrates the flight, airport transfer, and museum arrival on the same day as a fixed professional commitment. Thursday morning removes the need to leave the installation on a deadline. Even if work runs until 6:30 or 7:00 Wednesday, you can complete sign-off and return to the hotel without jeopardizing the flight.
Would the Wednesday 7:10 return save a hotel night if I arrive Monday?

Yes. Monday through Wednesday would require two hotel nights, while a Thursday morning return requires three. The airfare for Monday outbound plus Wednesday evening return is $301, which is $17 less than the Monday-through-Thursday 7:00 a.m. pairing. The meaningful added cost is therefore one hotel night, not the airfare difference.
That makes the Wednesday return look like false economy. The installation team has run late before, and I am the one responsible for completing the handoff paperwork.

Agreed. In that situation, the Wednesday 7:10 p.m. flight creates a deadline exactly where your assignment is most likely to vary. Monday evening outbound with a Thursday morning return is the more defensible pairing. Between the Thursday flights, 7:00 a.m. minimizes time away and costs $29 less, while 9:15 a.m. avoids a very early departure from the hotel.
Use the 7:00 a.m. Thursday return for the comparison. I can manage an early airport run. Are there seats available on those Delta flights?

Yes. The Monday 6:10 p.m. outbound currently has several standard seats available, including windows in the middle and rear of the main cabin. The Thursday 7:00 a.m. return also has standard window and aisle seats available. Preferred seats nearer the front cost extra on each segment.
Choose standard window seats when we book. I prefer a window seat whenever there is a choice; there is no need to pay extra just to sit farther forward.

I’ll apply standard window seats to both segments if they remain available. The current pairing is Monday, July 20, ATL to STL nonstop at 6:10 p.m., and Thursday, July 23, STL to ATL nonstop at 7:00 a.m., for $318 round trip before any bag fee. I have not booked it.
Before we settle on it, tell me what hotel dates this would create and whether the early return changes where I should stay.

The flight pairing creates a three-night hotel stay: check in Monday, July 20, and check out Thursday, July 23. For the 7:00 a.m. flight, you would want to leave the hotel at roughly 5:15 a.m. A hotel near the museum keeps Tuesday and Wednesday simpler; the pre-dawn ride from Forest Park to STL is generally about 20 minutes, so the early departure does not by itself justify moving to an airport hotel for the final night.

Good. Anchor the hotel search to Monday through Thursday near the museum. Do not book the flight yet because I need the registrar to confirm the installation dates, but this is the itinerary I want priced against lodging.

The hotel search will be anchored to check-in Monday, July 20 and check-out Thursday, July 23, near the Saint Louis Art Museum. The working flight itinerary is Delta nonstop ATL-STL Monday at 6:10 p.m., returning nonstop Thursday at 7:00 a.m., currently $318 round trip, with standard window seats to be selected if available. Nothing has been booked or held, and registrar confirmation remains outstanding.
